section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the distinction between solar years and lunar months, and questions why Nissan is called the head of the months of the year.
section.t: "This month is for you the head of the months, it is the first for you of the months of the year."
Now,
the well-known statement of the Ibn Ezra is known:
"The moon has no year at all, just as the sun has no month at all."
That is,
the division of time called a year pertains to the sun,
for during a year the sun travels and revolves until it returns to its original place,
and then it revolves again once more, etc.,
therefore it is called "shanah," from the word "shinui" (change/repetition)
(that the same thing returns and is repeated once more),
but from month to month nothing changes in its course.
And the division of time called a month pertains to the moon,
for its course until it returns to the first point is the duration of a month,
but from year to year nothing changes in its course.
Based on this, we must understand what is written: "This month... for the months of the year,"
which mentions the matter of a year in relation to months.
Also, we must understand
what is written about Rosh Chodesh Nissan: "This month is for you the head of the months, it is the first...,"
yet the first of Tishrei is Rosh HaShanah.
And as explained in Likkutei Torah,
the precise meaning of "Rosh HaShanah"
(and not "beginning of the year"),
is that just as the head includes the life-force of all the limbs of the body,
so too Rosh HaShanah includes the life-force of the entire year,
for even though there is a renewal of life-force each day,
as the saying,
"Who renews in His goodness every day, constantly, the work of creation,"
and not only each day but even each moment,
nevertheless,
there is an established order in the drawing down and renewal of life-force,
that first there is the drawing down of the general life-force on Rosh HaShanah,
and it is then divided into twelve heads of months,
and from Rosh Chodesh it is drawn to all the days of the month.
And it is explained at length and in more detail in Ateret Rosh,
that there are two aspects of "head,"
the first,
that the life-force of all the limbs of the body is first included in the head and from there is drawn to all the limbs,
and the second,
that even after the life-force has already been drawn to all the particular limbs, the head is their director,
and as explained in Tanya,
that even now
(after the drawing of life-force from the head to all the limbs)
the nourishment of the nails is drawn from the brain in the head,
and these two aspects also exist in Rosh HaShanah.
Based on this, we must understand what it means that Rosh Chodesh Nissan is "the head of the months, the first"
("first" also meaning "head")
"it is for you of the months of the year,"
that is,
that Rosh Chodesh Nissan is analogous to the aspects in the analogy of the head in its simple sense,
yet the aspect of Rosh HaShanah is on the first of Tishrei.
